recipes.name: Kris' Amazing Shredded Mexican Beef
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 pound) beef bottom round roast or other lean roast
1 (7 ounce) can chipotle peppers in adobo sauce, or to taste

steps.text: Trim the roast of any excess fat, and cut into four pieces. Rub with black pepper, and place into a slow cooker. Add the onions, green chiles, chili powder, cayenne pepper, garlic powder, cumin, chipotle peppers, and beef bouillon. Pour in enough water to cover 1/3 of the roast.
Cover, and cook on High until the meat begins to fall apart, about 8 hours. Add water if needed to keep the roast from drying out.

Turn the slow cooker to Low, and remove meat to a large bowl with a slotted spoon. Shred the meat into bite-sized pieces using two forks. Return the meat to the slow cooker; cook about 20 minutes to reheat before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Kris' Amazing Shredded Mexican Beef
raw_recipe.description: My husband grew up in southern California, and he says this shredded Mexican beef is the best he's ever had. Use it in burritos, tacos, salads and more.

review.reviewBody: As a "gringo" who loves authentic Mexican food, this was absolutely wonderful! I varied the recipe only a bit, using a bone-in chuck roast that weighed about 2 1/2 pounds. I reduced the quantities of most of the other ingredients about one third (not exactly, just eyed it). I had chipotles in adobo in freezer (great way to store them if you don't use a whole can) and I threw in 4-5 fat ones. I also used home made beef stock instead of water and beef bouillon. Cooked for about 7 hours then shredded and returned to the juices as stated. Served on flour tortillas with some jalapeno poppers (from this site) and some beans. A fiesta in your mouth!

Fabulous and spicy! May reduce the cayenne next time for those that need a little less heat. I used 1c water w/ 1 tsp Better than Boullion, blended seasonings(along with 1 1/2 tsp salt) with the chilies, chipotles, and onion. Cut beef into 2" cubes, browned, deglazed with the broth and cooked in the Instant Pot for 80 minutes & NR.

I only used a half can of chipotles and eliminated the cayenne pepper because my 80yo mother doesn’t like anything spicy. Once I took the chunks of meat out of the crockpot and shredded it, I tasted it. It was still too spicy. I dumped the juice from the crockpot. I put the shredded beef and some beef broth into a pan to keep the meat moist. At this point it was mild enough for us to eat. I then stirred in some frozen corn for color. My family could not get enough of this. I served it with tortillas, rice, fresh salsa, shredded cheese and cilantro. They want to know when I will make it again!

I'm glad I read the reviews. It would have been much, much too hot with a full can of the adobo chilies. I used 3 chilies and saved the rest. It's still quite spicy--and I usually like spicy foods. Knowing there would be a possibility of it being too spicy, I reduced the cayenne by a half. Also, it doesn't need an actual slow cooker. I used a heavy Dutch oven type pot and cooked on low heat for 5 hours. It is very tender and tasty. Great in a flour tortilla.

I have made this very similar recipe several times, and it is my go-to way of making shredded beef. If the heat is too much, you can reserve the actual jalapenos and just use the adobo sauce, squeezing any extra sauce from the Chiles. Remember, it's the pepper vein that adds the heat, not the seeds. (Several folks commented they painstakingly remove the seeds) I have also adapted to use the Instant Pot. Still amazing!

Followed recipe almost. Read footnote and kept all spices the same level as recommended for a 4 pound roast even if your using a smaller roast. Two changes. I increased the Chipotle peppers from 1/4 to 1/2 the can for a smaller roast and I used can of 16 oz Beef broth (eliminating the beef bouillon and water option) NO NEED TO ADD ANY SALT. as some reviews suggested. This was spicy but not flaming hot. Also when using a 2 pound roast you don't need to cook it for 8 hours. I was able to pull it apart in 6 hours, lower it to low as instructed and put the shredded beef back into the pot. Saving the drippings for a spicy chicken soup. Waste not; Want not. A family favorite

I smoked a London Broil Low and slow for 4 hours then transferred it to the crockpot and followed directions but cooked on low till it fell apart (about 4 more hours ) It was a little spicy! So we used it to top baked potatoes, added sour cream and pickled purple cabbage with ginger and cilantro. It was a hit!!!

I'll happily add my 5-star rating to all the others! I made this for dinner last night to use in burritos. I used bottom round (that's what I had) and I cooked it in the oven because I didn't have enough time to do it in the slow cooker. I followed the advice of others and added only about 4 chipotle peppers (removed the seeds from the largest) and I cut the amount of cayenne pepper in half too. I like spicy but didn't want to overdo it the first time trying the recipe. The sauce was spicy enough, but the meat was just perfect! My husband said it tasted as good as our favorite Mexican restaurant (that charges a LOT for an all-meat burrito). I had plenty of leftovers and I can't wait to use them - maybe in a tamale pie. This would also be a great recipe to make Italian Beef sandwiches just by changing up the spices and the type of peppers. It would also be great to use in BBQ Beef sandwiches (pulled beef!). Thanks so much for posting this recipe - it's a winner and we LOVED it! Can't wait to check out some of your other recipes.

Made this last week for my family. Heeded the warning about the heat so only added 4 medium chipotles. It was too hot so I simmered only the meat with added water in a frying pan which toned it down a bit. Served in flour tortillas with refried beans, cheese, cilantro, tomatoes, and sour cream with a squeeze or fresh lime juice. It still had what we call "an afterburn." I made it again this week for my sister's family with no cayenne and 4 medium chipotles. That was perfect and everyone loved it! I did remove the chipotles from the crock but put the shedded meat back
into the juices/marinade. Served the same as above. Froze the rest for another time. Will try this in enchiladas in the future. Thanks for sharing!

Update: I bumped my rating from 4 to 5 stars! We made these again over the weekend and I used the entire can of peppers in Adobe sauce (still removing the whole peppers before shredding the beef) it was not too spicy for us and the flavor was incredible! My kids have already requested this again!
First Review: I found the recipe last night and made them tonight!! Yummy! I used a 3 lb roast and only 3 peppers, I did pour a little of the Adobe sauce in before starting the crock pot. I also used 2 fresh cloves of garlic, minced, instead of the powdered and beef stock in place of water and the bullion cube. The whole family enjoyed them. We served them with sour cream, freshly grated cheese, diced tomatoes and slices of avocado. THANKS for a great recipe. This one is a keeper!

This was very good and had a lot of flavor. I cut the roast down to 2 pounds but kept everything else the same except the chipotle peppers (I used two peppers). It was one the verge of being too spicy for my family, but was pretty close to being perfect. I cooked it on low for ten hours in lieu of cooking it on high for eight hours, as the recipe indicated. The roast literally fell apart and was cooked perfectly. We served on baked corn tortillas with lettuce, monterray jack cheese, tomatoes, sour cream and guacamole. It made for a wonderful meal! Thanks for sharing your recipe, happygirl820!
This has become a family favorite. I don’t return the meat to the slow cooker after shredding - if people want some additional spice, I reserve some of the mixture for them to poor over their portion

I've been making this for years. I just searched and searched to see if I could find it, so I could print it. Success!! I use London Broil as my beef and 2-3 chipotle peppers. It comes out great. I'm from San Diego. Everywhere I move to has terrible Mexican food. This is my solution.
My entire family loves this recipe, I made it with chuck roast because that was on sale when I first made it, so I’ve stuck with that. Super simple but oh so tasty.

I've made this several times and love it!!! Initially I made it according to the directions; but then tried it with a chuck roast, which I preferred over the bottom round roast. To me it was more moist and tender.
ThIs recipe is AMAZING. Rarely do I find a recipe that is this good without any tweaking. I make it with rice and corn salsa. If it is too spicy, a little sour cream is all it takes. Highly recommend

I like heat, and I cut the chipotles back to 1 pepper and a spoonful of sauce, but it was still a bit much. Next time I think I'll omit the cayenne pepper all together. Put mine in a low-carb wrap with diced tomatoes, avocado, and cheese. Served with homemade applesauce and steamed broccoli.
Delicious! I’ve been making the highest rated taco recipe on here and decided to switch it up and this is just as good or maybe even better !

I feel bad for leaving a low review because I know that a lot of people would really like this recipe. But I didn’t care for it at all. It was way too spicy. To give an accurate assessment of my taste, at a typical Thai restaurant I prefer 2 stars and max out at 3 stars for heat.

I loved it! I saw this recipe and tried it out for making super nachos, because presentation is everything to my kids and tacos are hit or miss. My wife has no spice tolerance beyond black pepper, but did tell me the flavor was good. My son and I were the only ones left to finish it all off and we enjoyed every bit of it. Even made omelets with it the next morning so good!
